fields.meta_title: Employee Satisfaction Survey, Scored by Topic | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee satisfaction survey that scores pay, managers, workload and schedules by site and shift, with confidential results. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Satisfaction Survey Scored by Topic
fields.hero_description: Tell Emergent who works for you and which parts of the job you want rated. You get the questions, a score for each topic by site and shift, and every response stored in your own database.
fields.features_subheading: An employee satisfaction survey asks how content people are with the parts of the job you control, such as pay, benefits, their manager and their schedule.
fields.feature_1:
One statement per part of the job

Emergent writes a satisfaction item for each topic you name, such as pay, benefits, workload or schedule, then adds one overall question about the job as a whole.
fields.feature_2:
Percent satisfied for every topic

Each topic is scored as the share of people who chose 4 or 5 on a 1-5 scale. The average sits underneath, since a split team and a lukewarm one can share an average.
fields.feature_3:
Confidential or anonymous, up front

Before the first question, the survey states which it is and who sees what. A group below your minimum, such as five answers, shows no results but counts in the total.
fields.feature_4:
Splits by site, shift and role

Upload a roster with each person's location, shift and role, or sync it from your HRIS by API. The survey never asks for those details, which keeps small groups harder to spot.
fields.feature_5:
A follow-up only after a low score

When someone answers 1 or 2 on a topic, one open question asks what would change their rating. Each comment is tagged to its topic and listed beside that topic's score.
fields.feature_6:
Your survey as code in GitHub

Export the whole survey, its response tables and its dashboards to your own GitHub repository. Run it on your servers, edit it by hand or keep prompting Emergent for changes.
fields.why_description: The tools below price per user or per employee, and responses stay on their platform. Emergent builds the employee satisfaction survey software itself, as an app whose code and data you keep.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every topic scored as a share of satisfied answers

A 30-question survey on seven topics goes to all 350 employees and stays open for 10 days. Each topic's score is the share of people who answered 4 or 5. Pay comes in last, and the comments under it repeat one complaint: annual raises trail what new hires are offered.
fields.tab_content_2:
Night shift gets its own staffing score

Nurses on every unit answer a nurse satisfaction survey of 18 questions on staffing, scheduling, their charge nurse and patient load. Results split by unit and by day or night shift. When fewer than half of one shift on a unit are satisfied with staffing, the unit's nurse manager gets an email with the counts and comments.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each principal reads only their own school

One teacher satisfaction survey link goes to teachers and support staff at nine schools in the district. Each principal sees their own school's results and nothing else, while the district office sees all nine. A school with fewer than five answers shows no results. Planning time scores lowest across the district.
fields.tab_content_4:
Remote and office staff, side by side

Remote and office staff answer the same 12 work satisfaction survey questions on workspace, equipment, software and focus time. The dashboard puts the two groups in adjacent columns. Remote staff rate home equipment lowest, and their comments become a list of requests for the IT lead, sorted by how often each one comes up.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Satisfaction Survey
fields.howto_description: Most of the work is picking topics you are prepared to change. The questions follow from that choice, and so does the report people get back.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the topics you can change
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write one plain item per topic
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give Emergent the brief in plain English
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the parts of the job leadership can act on this year: pay bands, benefits, schedules, tools, manager training. Leave out what you cannot touch. Asking about something you will not change tells people their answers go nowhere.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use statements such as "I am satisfied with my pay for the work I do" on a 1-5 scale from very dissatisfied to very satisfied. Add one overall item on the job as a whole, and keep open questions to two at most.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A confidential survey knows who answered and uses that for reminders and team splits. An anonymous one stores no identity, so reminders go to everyone. Pick one, then set the smallest group that can see its own results.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Say who gets the survey, which topics it covers, the scale, the privacy rule and how long it stays open. Emergent builds the survey, the response table and the dashboards from that description. Edits after launch are another prompt.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to a team of 10 or 15 people first and note how long it takes them. Read their comments for questions people misread or skipped, and fix that wording before the company-wide launch.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sort topics by percent satisfied and begin at the bottom. Open the comments under each low topic, then compare groups. A score that is low on one shift or at one site usually needs a local fix rather than a new policy.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Name one change per low topic
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish company results within a few weeks of closing. For the two lowest topics, name one change each, with an owner and a date. Next year, run the same items with the same wording to see whether those scores moved.

plan.angle: The top 10 is question lists (HRMorning, Voxco, easy-feedback) and fixed templates (SurveyMonkey, SurveyHero, BlockSurvey, Honestly). None shows how to score satisfaction by topic or how to split it by shift, school or work location. This page answers the PAA questions on questions, anonymity and scores, keeps satisfaction (contentment with pay, manager, workload and conditions) apart from engagement, and shows four working surveys a company owns as an app.
tab_stories: A 30-question company-wide survey of 350 people reports each topic as the share of satisfied answers, and pay comes in lowest of seven topics.

A school district surveys teachers and support staff at nine schools, each principal sees only their own school, and planning time is the lowest item district-wide.
Remote and office staff rate their workspace, equipment and software side by side, and the gap on home equipment becomes a list for the IT lead.

claims_to_source: Job satisfaction measures how content people are with the job and its conditions, while engagement measures commitment and discretionary effort
Spector's Job Satisfaction Survey has 36 items across nine facets, including pay, promotion, supervision, benefits and coworkers, on a six-point agreement scale
A top-box or percent-favorable score is the share of answers in the top two points of the scale
A confidential survey links answers to identity while an anonymous survey stores no identity
Survey tools hide results for groups below a minimum number of answers
